questions.q: Which of these is NOT a function of the kidney?
questions.explain: Bile salts are made by the liver. The kidney excretes waste, regulates water, electrolytes and acid-base balance, and secretes erythropoietin, renin and calcitriol.

questions.q: What is the approximate blood flow to both kidneys per minute at rest?
questions.explain: The kidneys are about 0.5% of body weight but receive roughly a quarter of the cardiac output.

open.q: What is the approximate blood flow to both kidneys per minute at rest?

questions.q: Which hormone made by the kidney stimulates red cell production?
questions.explain: Peritubular interstitial cells release erythropoietin in response to hypoxia. Loss of it in kidney failure causes anaemia.

open.q: Which hormone made by the kidney stimulates red cell production?

questions.q: Which active form of vitamin D is made by the kidney?
questions.explain: The proximal tubule hydroxylates 25-hydroxycholecalciferol at the 1 position, giving calcitriol.

open.q: Which active form of vitamin D is made by the kidney?

questions.q: What is the functional unit of the kidney?
questions.explain: Each nephron has a renal corpuscle and a tubule, and forms urine on its own.

open.q: What is the functional unit of the kidney?

questions.q: Roughly how many nephrons are in each human kidney?
questions.explain: Each kidney has about 1 to 1.3 million nephrons. They cannot regenerate, so loss is permanent.

open.q: Roughly how many nephrons are in each human kidney?

questions.q: What does the renal corpuscle consist of?
options: Bowman's capsule and loop of Henle
questions.explain: The renal corpuscle is the filtering part of the nephron: a tuft of capillaries inside a double-walled capsule.

open.q: What does the renal corpuscle consist of?

questions.q: Which cells form the visceral layer of Bowman's capsule?
questions.explain: Podocytes wrap around the glomerular capillaries with foot processes, leaving filtration slits between them.

open.q: Which cells form the visceral layer of Bowman's capsule?

questions.q: Which nephron type has the long loop of Henle that dips deep into the medulla and is important for concentrating urine?
questions.explain: Only about 15% of nephrons are juxtamedullary, but their long loops and vasa recta create the medullary gradient.

open.q: Which nephron type has the long loop of Henle that dips deep into the medulla and is important for concentrating urine?

questions.q: The brush border is a feature of which part of the nephron?
questions.explain: Microvilli greatly increase the surface area for the large reabsorptive load of the proximal tubule.

open.q: The brush border is a feature of which part of the nephron?

questions.q: What are the three layers of the glomerular filtration membrane?
options: Continuous endothelium, basement membrane and tight junctions
Fenestrated endothelium, basement membrane and podocyte filtration slits
Fenestrated endothelium and Bowman's capsule only
questions.explain: The negatively charged basement membrane and slit diaphragms restrict albumin and larger proteins.

open.q: What are the three layers of the glomerular filtration membrane?
accept: fenestrated endothelium, basement membrane, slit pores

questions.q: Which cells of the juxtaglomerular apparatus secrete renin?
options: Juxtaglomerular (granular) cells of the afferent arteriole
questions.explain: JG cells are modified smooth muscle cells with renin granules.

open.q: Which cells of the juxtaglomerular apparatus secrete renin?

questions.q: The macula densa is part of the wall of which tubule segment?
questions.explain: Macula densa cells sense NaCl delivery to the distal tubule and signal the glomerulus.

open.q: The macula densa is part of the wall of which tubule segment?

questions.q: Name a stimulus for renin release.
options: A rise in renal arterial pressure
Increased NaCl delivery to the macula densa
A fall in renal arterial pressure
questions.explain: Renin is released by low pressure in the afferent arteriole, low NaCl at the macula densa, and sympathetic (β1) stimulation.

open.q: Name a stimulus for renin release.
open.a: A fall in renal arterial pressure (also low NaCl at the macula densa and sympathetic stimulation)

questions.q: Renin acts on which substrate?
questions.explain: Renin cleaves angiotensinogen from the liver to form angiotensin I.

open.q: Renin acts on which substrate?

questions.q: Which enzyme converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II?
questions.explain: ACE works mainly on the endothelium of lung capillaries. ACE inhibitors block this step.

open.q: Which enzyme converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II?

questions.q: Which is NOT an action of angiotensin II?
options: Stimulation of ADH release and thirst
questions.explain: Angiotensin II stimulates aldosterone secretion from the adrenal cortex.

questions.q: Name the vessels, in order, that blood passes through from the afferent arteriole onwards.
options: Efferent arteriole → glomerulus → afferent arteriole → peritubular capillaries
Interlobular artery → peritubular capillaries → glomerulus → efferent arteriole
Afferent arteriole → glomerulus → efferent arteriole → peritubular capillaries
Arcuate artery → efferent arteriole → glomerulus → afferent arteriole
questions.explain: Blood passes through two capillary beds in series, the glomerular and the peritubular.

open.q: Name the vessels, in order, that blood passes through from the afferent arteriole onwards.
accept: afferent arteriole, glomerulus, efferent arteriole, peritubular capillaries

questions.q: Between which two kinds of vessels does the glomerular capillary bed lie?
questions.explain: This arrangement lets the kidney keep a high glomerular pressure (about 60 mmHg).

open.q: Between which two kinds of vessels does the glomerular capillary bed lie?

questions.q: Which vessels supply the renal medulla and help preserve its concentration gradient?
questions.explain: The vasa recta act as countercurrent exchangers.

open.q: Which vessels supply the renal medulla and help preserve its concentration gradient?

questions.q: What fraction of the plasma entering the glomeruli is filtered (filtration fraction)?
questions.explain: GFR 125 ml/min divided by renal plasma flow about 625 ml/min gives about 0.2.

open.q: What fraction of the plasma entering the glomeruli is filtered (filtration fraction)?

questions.q: Over roughly what range of mean arterial pressure does renal autoregulation keep blood flow constant?
questions.explain: Within this range, renal blood flow and GFR barely change. Below it, filtration falls.

open.q: Over roughly what range of mean arterial pressure does renal autoregulation keep blood flow constant?

questions.q: Which two mechanisms are mainly responsible for renal autoregulation?
questions.explain: Stretch of the afferent arteriole causes it to constrict (myogenic). Macula densa signals adjust the afferent arteriole (feedback).

open.q: Which two mechanisms are mainly responsible for renal autoregulation?

questions.q: Which substance's clearance is used to measure renal plasma flow?
questions.explain: PAH is almost completely removed from plasma in one pass, so its clearance approximates renal plasma flow.

open.q: Which substance's clearance is used to measure renal plasma flow?
